title: Measures to Prevent Further Fraudulent Claims for SkillsFuture
what_it_is: Measures to Prevent Further Fraudulent Claims for SkillsFuture

sections.label: SkillsFuture fraudulent claims questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Education about fraudulent SkillsFuture claims, counter-measures, review, investigation outcome, safeguards and staff suspension, noting over 4,400 false claims exceeding $2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) whether he can provide a detailed account of the recent spate of fraudulent claims from SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG); (b) what are the counter-measures taken; and (c) whether a full review will be undertaken to prevent future breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) what will be the measures taken to prevent future abuses of SkillsFuture claims without stifling the growth of the SkillsFuture movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) what is the outcome of the Government's internal investigation into the weakness of its controls over the $40 million scam on SkillsFuture claims; (b) whether there have been additional safeguards put in place since $2.2 million have been identified as false claims earlier in March 2017; (c) why did the rectification measures put in place from the earlier incident failed to prevent the recent occurrence; and (d) whether any staff or personnel have been suspended pending investigations on the lapse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In the first case, more than 4,400 individuals were found to have made false SkillsFuture Credit claims within a very short period last year, amounting to over $2 million.

sections.label: Second case $40 million
sections.summary: The second case involves $40 million of fraudulent claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The second case involves $40 million of fraudulent claims.

sections.label: Police seize cash and gold
sections.summary: The Police seized $6.7 million in cash and 11 kilogrammes of gold, and froze slightly more than $10 million in bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Police have also seized $6.7 million in cash and 11 kilogrammes of gold, and frozen slightly more than $10 million in bank accounts.

sections.label: SSG review and reskilling
sections.summary: SSG will review and rectify grant administration shortcomings, but the case should not detract from reskilling and upskilling the workforce amid technological disruptions and economic restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: SSG will do a thorough review and rectify any shortcomings in grant administration that it may have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But at the same time, we should not allow this case to detract from the important task of reskilling and upskilling the workforce in this period of technological disruptions and economic restructuring.

sections.label: Old numbers re-reported
sections.summary: The passage asks whether old numbers will be taken out and adjusted numbers re-reported, stating such numbers cannot be counted as training honestly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will some old numbers be taken out and the adjusted numbers re-reported?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We cannot count those numbers as training; that would not be honest.

sections.label: System capability gap remedy
sections.summary: The passage states the system has a big capability gap today, that this could and should have been prevented, and necessary actions will be taken to remedy it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The bottom line is this: the system has a big capability gap today, this could have been prevented and it should have been prevented, and we will take the necessary actions to remedy this.

sections.label: Interagency Task Force fraud review
sections.summary: The Interagency Task Force will review the fraud case, identify system gaps, implement measures, and examine structure, personnel and reporting lines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, on the Interagency Task Force, I do not have the terms of reference with me, but essentially, it has to, firstly, review the entire circumstances of the fraud case, how it happened; secondly, what are the gaps in our system today that led to us not being able to detect this and led to us detecting it so late; third, implement the measures; and fourth, to take a hard look at the whole structure and system, and what are the changes we need to do, including personnel, organisational reporting lines.
